prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
[goal] Deliver a playable 95-era-style archery game in ./game/index.html.
[action] Wrote a single-file canvas game: mouse aims, hold+drag back to draw, release to fire; balloons float up, pop physics + particles, score, 3 lives, start/lose overlay, WebAudio sounds (twang, pop, thud, game over), gravity arrows.
[result] Verified in a headless browser: page loads, overlay shows, START works, simulated mousedown/move/up fires an arrow, state updates (score 0, lives 3, overlay hides). No console errors observed. Note: screenshots could not be read (image input unavailable), so visual polish is verified by code, not by eye.
[next] None; assumptions: unlimited arrows, escapes cost a life, 30 pts for small balloons / 10 for big ones.
